item.description: Justin Herbert has taken responsibility for the Los Angeles Chargers’ lack of production, saying players must perform better as the team searches for answers. Head coach Jim Harbaugh has retained the coordinator, while Herbert said players must do more to turn opportunities into points. Chargers HC maintains confidence in OC Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert defended offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel , saying players must take responsibility for their performance. With the Chargers struggling to score consistently, Herbert said success depends on players carrying out their assignments rather than blaming the coaching staff. item.title: Zverev seals world number one spot after win
item.description: Alexander Zverev is the 30th man to become the ATP world number one [Getty Images] Alexander Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner as the men’s world number one at his earliest opportunity after reaching the quarter-finals in Vienna. Germany’s Zverev was already guaranteed to finish 2026 as the ATP’s leading player, but made sure he will rise to the summit on Monday with a 6-4 7-5 win over Tallon Griekspoor at the Erste Bank Open. Zverev, 29, is the second German to reach the pinnacle of the men's tour after Boris Becker in 1991. The achievement is a testament to his body of work this year, having won two Grand Slam titles and 64 of his 80 matches. "It's been a wait but sometimes you have to wait for the best things in life," said Zverev, who is the second oldest man to top the rankings for the first time. "I'm super happy, super thrilled - I have no words for this year." At the start of the year it seemed unthinkable that anybody other than Sinner or Carlos Alcaraz would become world number one. But the dominant duo have missed large chunks of this season through injury, opening the door for Zverev - who won the French Open and US Open titles with at least one of the pair absent - to take over. Going into 2026, Alcaraz led the rankings with 12,050 points, closely followed by Sinner on 11,500. The pair's duopoly - splitting all of the eight Grand Slam titles in 2024 and 2025 between them - was illustrated by the huge gap to the rest of the field. Third-ranked Zverev had 5,110 points - closer numerically to the 2,221st player in the world than the top two. Both his major triumphs came without having to face Sinner or Alcaraz, and he did not face a top-10 player until beating Ben Shelton in the New York final. As the season entered its final stretch, Zverev achieved what many thought was impossible by securing the year-end number one ranking when Alcaraz lost in Shanghai on 12 October. Zverev knew he still could not overtake Sinner until 2 November at the earliest, but beat Griekspoor to become the first man other than Sinner and Alcaraz to top the rankings since Novak Djokovic in June 2024. Zverev conceded he would "maybe not" be the world's best player if both his rivals were "healthy and at the top of their game". But he has efficiently beaten what has been in front of him, recording the greatest season of a career which had threatened to fall short of the lofty expectations placed on him since emerging as a teenage prodigy. item.title: Chancellor Lee Adams prepares for Special Olympics equestrian competition
item.description: Chancellor Lee Adams has joined a team of 12 athletes from Victory Farm in Gastonia to train for the Special Olympics equestrian competition. The team traveled to the Tryon International Equestrian Center in Mill Spring, North Carolina, to compete in the Southeast Regional Equestrian Tournament. Adams lives with cerebral palsy and has ridden horses on and off for years as physical therapy. The training has strengthened his core and legs, enabling him to take steps without relying on his walker. Victory Farm Head Instructor Dory Pell emphasized that the event is a rigorous athletic competition rather than a passive exercise. “So many people assume that we put these riders on a horse and we lead them through a course or we lead them around the ring. It is no pony ride! It is a true competition where they have to learn skills and ability. They are going to work through challenges such as making their body do what they didn’t think it was capable of,” Pell said. ALSO READ: Chancellor Lee Adams turns 26 Chancellor Lee Adams competes in two separate divisions: showmanship and working trail. In showmanship, Adams must lead his horse, Dore-Ry, through a memorized course. The working trail division simulates riding through the woods. “And that is one that has a lot of different obstacles and patterns. He has to remember all the patterns and obstacles and execute them to perfection. In the proper order,” Pell said. During practice, Adams worked on navigating obstacles, including stopping on a raised wooden platform and commanding his horse, “Whoa! 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.” Pell praised his commitment during training sessions. “That young man is so devoted to getting this done that he just works and works and works. He never wants to stop. We’re the ones that have to stop him because he wants to make sure he gets it right,” Pell said, describing his effort as “It’s astounding.” Adams was born after a November 1999 attack orchestrated by his father, former Carolina Panthers player Rae Carruth. Carruth hired a gunman who shot Adams’ mother, Cherica Adams, while she was pregnant. Cherica Adams died from her injuries, but Chancellor Lee Adams survived the shooting. item.title: History of WNBA Finals winner-take-all games: How Dream-Valkyries are making Game 7 history
item.description: History of WNBA Finals winner-take-all games: How Dream-Valkyries are making Game 7 history originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The best two words in sports are Game 7, as the old adage goes. For the first time in its history, the WNBA will be able to put that proposition to the test. The WNBA Finals is headed to Game 7 after the Dream downed the Valkyries in an emotional — and highly contentious — Game 6. The league only recently transitioned to having its championship be decided through a best-of-seven series. Still, neutrals will be hoping Saturday's match lives up to some of its predecessors as an eye-catching winner-take-all tilt. With that, here's a look at the history of Game 7s (and other configurations of a winner-take-all finale) in the WNBA Finals. MORE: Cathy Engelbert avoids season-defining nightmare as Dream force WNBA Finals Game 7 History of WNBA Finals Game 7s Regardless of the result, Saturday's matchup will make WNBA history as the first-ever Game 7 in league history. That's not to say there hasn't been winner-take-all matches in past championship series. In fact, the WNBA Finals has been littered with do-or-die contests. The league moved to a best-of-seven format in the title series last year. Before that, the WNBA Finals were contested over five games. The league initially installed a one-game championship before settling on a three-game arrangement in 1998. That format formally fell out of favor in 2005. While most WNBA Finals have tended to avoid a winner-take-all finale, there has been more than a few that have taken hold of the spotlight over the years. In 2024, the Liberty bested the Lynx in overtime of Game 5, benefitting from Sabrina Ionescu's game-tying triple at the end of regulation. With the win, New York claimed its first-ever WNBA title. The 2016 iteration of the competition saw the Sparks down the Lynx. Los Angeles secured the victory via a last-second basket from Nneka Ogwumike. item.title: Tom Brady Brings New Card Store To Pittsburgh
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Tom Brady is opening a trading card store in the heart of Pittsburgh, a city that hates him. This move feels like a bold play for the business side of sports. The new location sits at 1659 Smallman St. in The Terminal. It marks the 20th retail spot for the brand called CardVault by Tom Brady per Chain Store Age . The grand opening happens this Sunday morning. Fans can buy, sell, and trade cards right there in the Strip District. The store carries items from big names like Topps, Panini, and Upper Deck. You can find Pokémon cards and Magic: The Gathering packs too. People can even send their cards to get graded by pros at PSA, Beckett, and SGC. The shop stays open every day from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It is a place for collectors to meet and swap gear. This is not just a shop; it is a hub for the hobby. Why Pittsburgh? Pittsburgh has a huge fan base that loves sports more than almost any other city. Chris Costa, the co-founder of the brand, sees this clearly. He said, “Pittsburgh is one of America’s great sports cities, and we’re excited to bring CardVault to its passionate community of fans and collectors.” The team behind the store calls it a natural market. They want to grow their business by adding more shops across the country. The location is a smart spot for a new business. The Strip District draws crowds every weekend. It fits the vibe of a place where people love to collect things. Costa added, “Our 20th store reflects the momentum we’re building nationwide as we introduce a new generation of collectors to the hobby.” This shows they plan to keep growing fast. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) ATLANTA - Draymond Green is a truth teller. Just ask the Golden State Valkyries . Green, who has been in plenty of Game 7s during his long NBA career, warned the Valkyries before their potential WNBA Finals close-out Game 6, that it would be "the hardest game they've ever played in their lives. "Three (wins) is a long way from four." As it turns out, three wins is about 2200 air miles and three time zones away from four wins. Playing an early morning game, by their body clock, the Valkyries were on their way to getting blown out before your coffee finished brewing. They ended up losing Game 6 to the Atlanta Dream, 80-69 . And now the series is all tied up, heading back to Chase Center for a Halloween Night Game 7 on Saturday. Thursday was the first Game 6 in WNBA history. Game 7 will also be a first ever. So get out your lavender wigs and wings, your plastic swords and helmets. Dress up like a Valkyrie. Bring your A-game. Because it's going to be an all-fans on deck situation. A winner-take-all Game 7, the first time a Bay Area team has played a Game 7 at home for a championship since Green and the Warriors played one at Oracle Arena in 2016. And you may have blocked out the memory of how that one turned out. Before the game began, head coach Natalie Nakase said she was well caffeinated, with a double espresso (her order includes vanilla, cinnamon and brown sugar). But her players - wearing their non-threatening white uniforms - looked like they were sleep-walking. They fell into a 19-point hole in the first quarter, saw it grow to 25 points in the second quarter and allowed the Dream to shoot 53% from the three-point line in the first half, when they made 15. item.title: Nolan Arenado Nearing Major Career Change for Diamondbacks
item.description: Nolan Arenado Diamondbacks Getty Arizona Diamondbacks third baseman Nolan Arenado may make a major career change for the team ahead of next season. Arenado, a 10-time Gold Glover third baseman, has never played another position on the baseball diamond aside from his customary 3B. He has played 1,876 games in his MLB career at third base, plus 53 games at designated hitter. However, that may change next year, as the Diamondbacks are considering moving the 35-year-old California native to first base in 2027. Diamondbacks May Move Nolan Arenado to 1st base Per Diamondbacks general manager Mike Hazen, the team is toying with the idea of moving Arenado across the diamond next year from 3B to 1B. “We’ve talked about Nolan playing some first base, so that might be something we take a look at,” Hazen told MLB.com . According to the Diamondbacks GM, the move would be to help with navigating wear and tear on Arenado’s body, as he is getting into the latter years of his Baseball Hall of Fame career. “I think it’s taken a toll on him physically a little bit. So we’re trying to be mindful of that,” Hazen said. Per Hazen, Arenado is open to playing 1B in winter ball to help him learn the position, exhibiting his dedication to his craft. “He wants to go play. He’s said, ‘I’ve never played winter ball, I want to go.’ And so, I was like, ‘Look, (Geraldo) Perdomo goes and plays winter ball every year for a couple weeks, and he swears that it really helps set him up for the season. So not being a pitcher and being a veteran position player, I trust that you’re gonna take care of what you need to take care of, and I don’t have an issue with it.’ I don’t know that it’s a done deal, but we were just talking about it,” Hazen said. As well, moving Arenado to 1B could potentially help Arizona look at a bigger pool of players in free agency, as they could sign a third baseman instead of a first baseman. “It could help us, depending on what’s out there in the market for available players, by giving us more flexibility. It opens the door for us, externally, to consider different ways to improve the team,” Hazen said. Nolan Arenado Had a Big Year for Arizona In Arenado’s first year in Arizona, he hit .255 with a .806 OPS and a 122 OPS+, indicating his bat was 22% above league average. He also hit 30 home runs, while being serviceable at third base. Hazen was incredibly impressed by what Arenado did this past season, after the Diamondbacks picked him up for cheap from the St. Louis Cardinals , who dumped part of his contract on Arizona for little in return, a trade that looks genius for the Diamondbacks in hindsight. “Incredible. He had a great year. You know, I think lost in some of the disappointment of not making the playoffs and (finishing) just out of it is some of the individual performances, like Arenado’s,” Hazen said. item.title: Celtics’ Paul George Earns Glowing Praise From Sam Hauser, Jordan Walsh
item.description: Paul George, Boston Celtics It’s only been a few months, but Paul George is already having a big impact on his Boston Celtics teammates. The veteran forward has become somewhat of a sounding board for Boston’s younger talent and veterans alike. Speaking to the media on Thursday, October 29, Sam Hauser detailed some of the lessons he’s learned from the 9-time All-Star since he arrived with the Celtics as part of the Jaylen Brown trade. “I think early on, I just asked him like, ‘How have you made it this long in the NBA?’” Hauser recalled, via Bobby Krivitsky. “…And I think, on the floor, he obviously, he’s very talented on the defensive side of the ball, and I think kind of just watching him from afar and how he gets steals, how his body positioning, angles, and all that has been pretty impressive to watch.” Hauser continued. “Obviously, he makes our defense really, really good when he’s out there…Every now and then it’s like, ‘Hey, what do you see on this? What can I do to help you on this?’ Kind of deferring to him.” George has had an immediate impact on the Celtics, especially on the defensive end, where he’s among the league leaders in deflections following the opening week of the season. Paul George Has Been Helping Jordan Walsh One member of the Celtics roster who has been benefiting from George’s presence is Jordan Walsh. The fourth-year forward has reportedly spent significant amounts of time working with and learning from Boston’s latest veteran star. On Thursday, Walsh gave further insight into what he’s been learning from George since his arrival. “He’s a really good defender as well, and so a lot of his advice, yeah, we talk about offense a lot, getting to your shot, being confident with it,” Walsh explained. “But there are certain closeout techniques and steal techniques that he does; I’m trying to figure out as well. So, using that in games as well has been helpful.” Walsh has found himself lining up next to George to begin the season. Joe Mazzulla has deployed the defense-first forward as Boston’s two-guard to begin the season, allowing him to set the defensive tone while continuing to develop his game on the fly. Paul George Has Two Years Left On His Contract George has two years remaining on the four-year $211.5 million deal he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in 2024. This season, he’s earning $54.1 million, while next season he could earn $56.5 million. However, George does have a player option on his deal ahead of next season. As such, he could opt out and choose to explore free agency. Or, he could seek a longer-term, more team-friendly deal to remain with the Celtics and challenge for a championship in the coming years. Of course, there’s also the chance he opts in for one final year of generational money. Whatever George chooses to do, it’s clear that his presence is having a positive effect on his new teammates. item.title: Isaiah Likely’s 41 catches give the Giants a matchup to exploit
item.description: Oct 18, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely (9) looks on after a game against the New Orleans Saints at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants found an offensive matchup they should keep feeding, even as their quarterback situation changes. Isaiah Likely has 41 catches through seven games, one short of his previous career high. Only two other tight ends have topped 40 receptions in their first seven games with a team, the Giants noted . That pace will invite record talk. The more useful question is how New York keeps the tight end involved when opponents devote extra attention to him and Malik Nabers. The Giants can create more than one matchup J.J. McCarthy supplied a different passing threat in his first Giants start, completing five passes of at least 20 yards against Houston. He also had five such completions in the late portion of the previous game. Those plays do not all belong to Likely, but they show why a defense cannot assume New York only wants short throws. Oct 18, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) celebrates with tight end Isaiah Likely (9) after scoring a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Likely’s value is in giving the quarterback an answer between those opportunities. His 41 catches are already close to the 42 he recorded at his previous career best with Baltimore, and his presence gives defenses another player to locate before focusing exclusively on Nabers. I’d keep moving Likely around and use two-tight-end looks when they fit the opponent. The goal is to make the defense declare whether it will treat him as a receiving threat or defend the run with heavier personnel. That’s my proposed approach; the staff has not announced a new package. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. A strong start still needs balance The alternative is to spread the field with more wide receivers and let Nabers dictate coverage. McCarthy’s downfield ability makes that appealing, particularly if a defense gives New York favorable one-on-one matchups outside. Likely’s current reception pace is not a guarantee he will break Jeremy Shockey’s franchise tight-end record of 74. Opponents adjust, targets vary, and the Giants still have to protect their quarterback. The point is not to force every throw to Likely. It is to preserve the threat he creates while McCarthy grows into the offense, especially with Philadelphia and Washington coming after the bye. item.title: Championship Dreams Crushed! 9 NASCAR Cup Drivers Officially Eliminated From Title Contention
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez The NASCAR Cup Series championship battle has taken a dramatic turn, and nine drivers are officially out of the running for the 2026 title. Following a wild afternoon at Talladega Superspeedway, several major names have seen their championship dreams come to an end, leaving the remaining contenders with even more pressure heading into Martinsville. The biggest storyline belongs to Kyle Larson, who pulled off an incredible victory at Talladega and took control of the championship standings. His win created a massive points advantage and officially eliminated nine drivers from championship contention. Nine Drivers See Their Championship Hopes End The nine drivers eliminated are William Byron, Chase Elliott, Ty Gibbs, Austin Cindric, Carson Hocevar, Bubba Wallace, Daniel Suárez, Ryan Preece and Chris Buescher. Several of those names make the list especially surprising. Byron, who drives for Hendrick Motorsports, finished second at Talladega but still couldn’t earn enough points to remain mathematically eligible for the championship. Elliott is another major name on the list. The former Cup Series champion entered the Chase hoping to compete for another title, but a difficult postseason has officially ended those hopes. Byron and Elliott’s eliminations also leave Larson as the only Hendrick Motorsports driver still eligible to win the championship. Other notable names include Wallace, Gibbs and Cindric, all of whom entered the postseason with hopes of making a serious championship run. Instead, they will now have to focus on finishing the season strong. Larson Takes Control of the Championship While nine drivers are officially eliminated, Larson is in the best position of anyone remaining. His unbelievable last-lap comeback at Talladega turned what looked like a difficult afternoon into a massive championship opportunity. Larson now holds a 73-point lead over Denny Hamlin with only two races remaining. The driver of the No. 5 Chevrolet can even clinch his third Cup Series championship at Martinsville if he scores enough points. The Pressure Is Only Getting Higher With nine championship contenders officially eliminated, the remaining drivers have very little room for mistakes. Martinsville could determine whether Larson celebrates another championship or whether his competitors manage to keep the battle alive for Homestead. For nine drivers, the championship dream is over. For everyone else, the fight is just getting started.

item.description: WNBA Finals Game 7 prediction: Why Angel Reese's Dream will beat Valkyries to win their first title originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Before this WNBA Finals series began, I picked the Atlanta Dream to knock off the Golden State Valkyries in six games. It would hardly make sense, then, for me to reverse course and pick the Valkyries to win Saturday's Game 7, even though they will begin the game as a slight favorite. In all seriousness though, the Dream's 80-69 victory in Atlanta on Thursday showed why, when firing on all cylinders -- or even most -- they should be able to withstand the hostile atmosphere inside Chase Center and ride the best player in the series to a Game 7 win. Why Reese and the Dream will take down the Valkyries The Angel Reese factor is a big one. Slowed significantly by Kiah Stokes in the middle of this series, Reese snapped back to life on Thursday and flirted with a triple-double. She registered 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists while setting the Finals record with 78 total rebounds. The Dream started fast, playing Game 6 at their tempo and forcing the Valkyries into a shootout that Golden State is not exactly equipped to handle. Gray scored a team-high 23 points on 8-of-12 shooting, including a 5-of-7 mark from three-point range, while Howard dropped 21 on 6-of-11 shooting with four made threes. In that game, Reese simply refused to let the Dream lose , the individual outshining the Valkyries' collective. Game 7 will be the same way. Atlanta will push the pace, and Golden State won't be able to establish its downtempo possession game. If that prediction holds true, the Dream will end the longest season in WNBA history with a championship on Halloween.
